Rashi on Berakhot 24b:11:1.hebrew: חוצץ בטליתו על צוארו - מה שיש מן הטלית ולמעלה מן כתפיו, מדביק בצוארו. ובישן ערום קאמר:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:11:1.english: He forms a barrier with his garment at his neck - Whatever there is of the garment above his shoulders, he presses against his neck. And it is speaking of [one who is] sleeping naked.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:17:1.hebrew: לדידי לא סבירא לי - לא הייתי מזקיקו להפסיק:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:17:1.english: As for me, I do not hold [this] - I would not have required him to interrupt.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:1:1.english: And touches his garment - To remove the louse that is biting him.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:1:2.hebrew: אבל לא היה מתעטף - אם נפלה טליתו כשהוא מתפלל, לא היה נוטלה ומתעטף, שלא להפסיק:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:1:2.english: But he would not wrap himself - If his prayer shawl fell while he was praying, he would not take it and wrap himself [in it], so as not to interrupt [his prayer].

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:1:3.hebrew: על סנטרו - מנטו"ן בלע"ז, שלא תראה פתיחת פיו:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:1:3.english: On his chin - Menton [chin] in Old French — so that the opening of his mouth will not be seen.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:20:1.hebrew: בחבלי השוא - בחבלים שאינם חזקים, אלא נוחין להנתק, הן מושכין העון על עצמם. אף זה, על ידי דבור בעלמא הוא נענש:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:20:1.english: With cords of vanity - With cords that are not strong, but rather easily snapped, they draw iniquity upon themselves. So too, this [person] is punished through mere speech.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:21:1.hebrew: ובדבר הזה - בשביל דבור זה שנזהרתם עליו, תאריכון ימים:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:21:1.english: And through this matter - Because of this speech that you were careful about, you will prolong [your] days.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:22:1.hebrew: היתה טליתו חגורה על מתניו - לכסותו ממתניו ולמטה, אע"פ שממתניו ולמעלה הוא ערום, קורא ק"ש:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:22:1.english: [If] his garment was tied around his waist - To cover him from his waist down — even though from his waist up he is naked, he may recite the Shema.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:2:1.hebrew: הרי זה מקטני אמנה - כאילו אין הקב"ה שומע תפלת לחש. ומגביה הרבה:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:2:1.english: This one is among those of little faith - As if the Holy One, blessed be He, does not hear a whispered prayer. And [as for "one who raises his voice," this means that] he raises [it] greatly.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:2:2.hebrew: הרי זה מנביאי השקר - דכתיב: ויקראו בקול גדול (מלכים א י״ח:כ״ח):
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:2:2.english: This one is among the false prophets - As it is written: “And they cried out with a loud voice” (I Kings 18:28).

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:3:1.hebrew: המגהק והמפהק - הרי זה מגסי הרוח, וי"א ניכר שהוא מכוער, גרסינן:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:3:1.english: One who belches and one who yawns - "He is among the uncouth, and some say: It is clear that he is repulsive" is our reading.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:4:1.english: Rather, sneezing against sneezing is difficult - For sneezing can only be involuntary.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:5:2.hebrew: ותקילא לי כי כולי תלמודאי - שקולה עלי וחביבה, לפי שהיה רגיל להתעטש:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:5:2.english: And it is as weighty to me as all my learning - [It is] of equal weight to me and precious, because he was accustomed to sneeze.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:5:3.hebrew: כשם שעושים לו נחת רוח - שהעטוש נחת רוח לאדם:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:5:3.english: Just as they give him pleasure - For sneezing is a pleasure to a person.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:5:4.hebrew: כך עושים לו נחת רוח מלמעלה - מן השמים, למלאת שאלתו:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:5:4.english: So too they give him pleasure from above - From Heaven, to fulfill his request.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:6:1.hebrew: אפשר כדרבי יהודה - להבליע באפרקסותו — סודר שבראשו, ושני ראשין תלויין בפניו:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:6:1.english: [It is] possible in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - To absorb [it] in his head covering — a scarf on his head, and its two ends hang down in front of his face.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:6:2.english: He cast it - He threw it.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:8:1.hebrew: מישתמיט מיניה - לא היה נראה אליו, לפי שהיה רבי אבא חפץ לעלות לא"י, ורב יהודה אוסר לו. לפיכך, לא היה נכנס לבית המדרש:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:8:1.english: Avoiding him - He would not appear before him, because Rabbi Abba wished to ascend to the Land of Israel, and Rav Yehuda forbade him. Therefore, he would not enter the study hall.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:8:2.english: And I will hear something from him - From the outside.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:8:3.english: From the house of assembly - From the study hall.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:9:2.hebrew: עד שיכלה הרוח - מגופו, שנודף מאותו רוח:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:9:2.english: Until the wind dissipates - From his body, which emits an odor from that wind.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:9:3.english: And returns to prayer - To the place where he stopped.

Rashi on Berakhot 24b:9:4.hebrew: ואומר - בתוך התפלה, דהא מופסקת ועומדת כבר על ידי הרוח. לפיכך, יכול להפסיק נמי ולומר דבר זה באמצע:
Rashi on Berakhot 24b:9:4.english: And he says - [He says this] in the midst of the prayer, for [the prayer] is already in a state of interruption on account of the wind [i.e., the flatulence]. Therefore, he may also interrupt and recite this matter in the middle.

Tosafot on Berakhot 24b:17:1.hebrew: אמר ליה לדידי לא סבירא לי - פירוש: משום תרתי מילי — חדא, דסבירנא דאינו חוזר לראש, דאמר רבי יוחנן (ר"ה דף ל"ד:): "שמע תשע תקיעות בתשע שעות יצא"; ועוד, דסבירא לי מניח ידו על פיו, ואם כן הוי ליה ראוי. אלא לדידך, דסבירא לך דחייב להפסיק, וכו':
Tosafot on Berakhot 24b:17:1.english: [Rava] said to him: "According to my view, I do not hold [so]" - Explanation: [This is] on account of two things: First, that I hold that one does not return to the beginning [after an interruption], as Rabbi Yoḥanan said (Rosh Hashanah 34b): "If one heard nine [shofar] blasts over nine hours, he has fulfilled [his obligation]"; and furthermore, that I hold that [one walking in filthy alleyways] places his hand over his mouth [and recites], and if so, he was fit [to recite]. Rather, according to your view, as you hold that one is obligated to interrupt, etc. [and was thus not fit to recite, he must return to the beginning].

Tosafot on Berakhot 24b:1:1.hebrew: וממשמש בבגדו - פרש"י: להעביר הכינה העוקצתו; "אבל לא מתעטף" — אם נפלה טליתו, ותרי מילי נינהו. ור"ח פי' דחדא מילתא היא. פי': "ממשמש בבגדו" — תקן שלא יפול מעל ראשו; אבל אם נפל מעל ראשו — לא היה מתעטף, שהרי היא הפסקה אם מתעטף, כיון שנפל לגמרי; אבל לתקן קצת שלא יפול — לא הוי הפסקה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 24b:1:1.english: “And he feels with his garment” - Rashi explained: [This means] to remove the louse biting him; “but he would not wrap himself” — [this applies] if his prayer shawl fell, and they are two [separate] matters. And Rabbeinu Ḥananel explained that it is a single matter. Explanation: “He feels with his garment” — he adjusts [it] so that it will not fall off his head; but if it fell off his head, he would not wrap himself [in it], for behold, it is an interruption if he wraps himself [in it] once it has fallen off completely; but adjusting [it] slightly so that it does not fall is not an interruption.

Tosafot on Berakhot 24b:20:1.hebrew: בחבלי השוא - כלומר: בחנם מושכים עליהם עון, כי טוב היה שלא היו מקיימין אותו כלל:
Tosafot on Berakhot 24b:20:1.english: "With cords of vanity" - That is to say, they draw iniquity upon themselves for naught, for it would have been better had they not fulfilled it [the mitzvah] at all.

Tosafot on Berakhot 24b:9:1.hebrew: ואומר רבון העולמים - מיד באמצע תפלתו, ואח"כ מתחיל ממקום שפסק:
Tosafot on Berakhot 24b:9:1.english: "And he says: Master of the universe" - [He says this] immediately, in the middle of his prayer, and afterward begins from the place where he stopped.
